newsitem.title: USA: Jewell must pass trial period if he works as a cop.
newsitem.headline: Jewell must pass trial period if he works as a cop.

text.p: A state law enforcement agency has said former Olympic bomb suspect Richard Jewell must undergo a year's probation if he returns to work as a policeman, his attorney Lin Wood said on Saturday.

The sanction was made by the Georgia Peace Officers Standards and Training Council (POST), which charged Jewell with failing to list a 1990 arrest for impersonating an officer on the request for certification he submitted to the agency later that same year.
The sanction stipulated Jewell's license as a law enforcement officer would enter a one-year probationary period upon his joining any Georgia police organisation.
Wood said that Jewell, a one-time county sheriff's deputy and college campus policeman, would like to find a job in a sheriff's office or police department in the Atlanta metropolitan area.

Jewell became the subject of worldwide media attention as the only named suspect in the July 27 bombing at the Atlanta Olympic Games, which killed two and injured more than 100. He later was cleared of suspicion by the Justice Department.
Wood said he planned to appeal the POST decision and, "we believe a reasonable person or panel will reverse it. It's another injustice inflicted upon him."
The POST decision stems from an incident which took place six years ago in an apartment complex outside Atlanta, where Jewell worked as a part-time security guard.

Quoting state records, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Saturday that Jewell got into a dispute with a local couple and threatened to arrest them. It said Jewell had claimed to be a sheriff's deputy from a nearby county, but was actually a county jailer and had not yet been certified as a police officer by POST.

Jewell was arrested on a felony charge for impersonating an officer but later pleaded guilty to a lesser count of disorderly conduct. He was sentenced to a year of probation and ordered to undergo a psychological evaluation.

The arrest was not listed on his Sept. 12, 1990, request for POST certification. Wood said the application had been filled out by one of Jewell's fellow county employees and that POST officials had been notified separately of the arrest. He said the application sought information about convictions only and was submitted months before the plea agreement.
